source_text: Τοῦ αὐτοῦ. Ναζιραῖον τὸ πεφυλαγμένον κατὰ τὴν Σύρων φωνὴν ὀνομάζει. Μὴ ἐξακολουθεῖν δὲ τῇ τάξει τῶν Ἰσραηλιτῶν τὸν Σαμψὼν ὁ Θεὸς προστάσσει, κατ᾿ ἐκεῖνο καιροῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν ξυρωμένων διὰ τὸ εὐσήμους εἶναι πρὸς πάντας.
thought_title: Nazirite as the guarded one and Samson's unshorn head
orientation: Origen is explaining the meaning of the term Nazirite and why God commanded Samson not to follow the Israelite custom of shaving the head.
pass_a_gloss: Of the same author. He names the Nazirite 'the guarded one' according to the Syrian tongue. And God commands Samson not to follow the order of the Israelites, at that time shaving the head, because they were to be conspicuous to all.

choices.why: The glossary requires Nazirite for this term.
Origen explicitly glosses the term as meaning 'the guarded one' in Syrian; the rendering preserves the passive perfect sense.
Keeps the literal sense of τάξις as order or arrangement, matching the source's contrast between Samson and Israelite custom.
Renders the purpose clause literally; εὔσημος means marked or conspicuous, and πρὸς πάντας means to all.
rejected: to be a sign to all

pass_b_english: He calls the Nazirite “the guarded one” in the Syrian language. God commands Samson not to follow the order of the Israelites, who at that time shaved their heads so as to be conspicuous to everyone.
